title: One phase transition in the hosted run
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Boolean machine with state set $Q$, let $\mathrm{upd}:T\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, and let $\mathrm{seek}$ be a two-tape Boolean machine with designated states $\mathrm{start},\mathrm{finish}\in S$. Choose a record-stage index $i$ whose stage is not a verdict stage, and configurations $c,c'$ of the corresponding phase machine on an input $x$. Suppose that running its row machine from $c$ for $t$ steps gives $c'$, that $c'$ has phase state $s'$, and that the phase-transition function sends $s'$ to an outcome $o$. Suppose also that before time $t$ every phase state reached has no phase transition, and that through time $t$ every work-head position stays within radius $r$ of a specified base position on each of the four tapes. Then the hosted record-step machine runs from the configuration obtained by adjoining phase index $i$ to $c$ to the configuration obtained by replacing the state of $c'$ with $o$, in $t+1$ steps, without visiting either verdict state before the final time; throughout these steps all four work-head displacements from the specified base positions are at most $r$.
